author: reek
body: The smallest thing that can tell whether a two-argument call places its arguments in the declared order. Subtraction is not commutative, so the answer names the order: seven minus two is five, and two minus seven is negative five. No recursion, no match, no tail call, no list.

author: reek
body: The second probe pairs a literal with a call, because that is the shape the parameter-order defect was first seen in and it takes a different branch of the two-argument emitter than two bare literals do.

author: reek
body: The same predicate that orders call arguments also drives `skip-save` in the binary-operand emitter, so a binary expression whose right operand is a nullary definition is the second shape it governs. Subtraction again, so the answer names the order rather than merely differing from it.
